- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) or volatile, model often overpredicts; reduce forecast by 1–4% to align with downward pressure.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–7 days post-spike.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 7-day average (e.g., < 70% of 7-day mean), consider mean reversion bias — add 1–3% to forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is weak or mixed, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: reduce forecast volatility by 20–40% if sentiment < 0.5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.3 → +0.6), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to anticipate sentiment shift.
